Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 26918 of 2024

Applicant :- Kalawati @ Kamlawati Verma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Shikher Trivedi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Shikher Trivedi, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Rajendra Prasad Singh,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 47 of 2022, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 323,
504, 506 & 406 of I.P.C., Police Station - Jhunsi, District - Prayagraj, during the pendency of trial.
3.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that similarly placed co-accused person,
Ghanshyam Verma, has already been enlarged on bail by another Bench of this Court vide order dated 05.03.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 5813 of 2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 5813 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
It is further Kalawati @ Kamlawati Verma vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137976305/
1 submitted that since the case of the applicant is at par to the co-accused, who has already been enlarged on bail, she is also entitled to be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity.
4.

entities.text: Kalawati @ Kamlawati Verma vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant has criminal history of 15 cases of similar nature.
The applicant has explained 12 of the said cases and in rest of three cases, she has yet to apply for bail wherein one case is under the Gangsters Act.
She is languishing in jail since 02.01.2024.

In case, the applicant is released on bail,
she will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.
5. The prayer for bail has been vehemently opposed by learned A.G.A.
However, the aforesaid factual aspect of parity to the co-accused has not been disputed by him.

6. In the case of Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648, the Supreme Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused may itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, (2020) 11 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In so far as criminal antecedents of the applicant is concerned, it is not the case of the State that applicant might tamper with or otherwise adversely influence the investigation, or that he might intimidate witnesses before or during the trial.
The State has also not placed any material that applicant in past attempted to evade the process of law.

If the accused is otherwise found to be entitled to bail, he cannot be denied bail only on the ground of criminal history, no exceptional circumstances on the basis of criminal antecedents have been shown to deny bail to accused, hence,
the Court does not feel it proper to deny bail to the applicant just on the ground that he had criminal antecedent.
8.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, evidence on record, pending trial and in the light of the judgement passed by this Court in Nanha S/o Nabhan Kha vs. State of U.P., 1993 Crl.L.J. 938 and the judgement passed by the Supreme Court in Paras Ram Vishnoi vs. The Director, Central Bureau of Investigation,
MANU/SCOR/22410/2021 coupled with the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case

sentences.text: , the Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case.
The bail application is allowed on the ground of parity.

9. Let the applicant- Kalawati @ Kamlawati Verma, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to Kalawati @ Kamlawati Verma vs State Of U.P. on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137976305/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
